transcript: Join me at the theater tonight I'm seeing Dark Noon at St Ann’s Warehouse. This show is part history lesson part horror movie it's the story of how Americans settled the Wild West told by seven South African actors when you walk in the set is literally just a dirt floor and a screen but over the course of 100 minutes an entire Old West town is constructed in front of you. This is a show that is actually incredibly hard to explain but an experience that you do not want to miss. It utilizes a lot of cameras. The whole thing is told in chapters and it makes these incredibly wild swings from absolutely on the floor hilarious to brutal and devastating. If you're in the front row there is audience participation you may get pulled into a saloon or a church service or a prison but I was riveted from the first minute on and afterwards they let you wander around and like explore the village and they even have a working train it is incredible. I've been thinking so much about this show since I saw it. It tackles so much American history but one of the most interesting parts is the epilogue where the South African actors share their personal experiences with Wild West movies St Ann’s never shies away from bold daring and important work and I'm so glad they are sharing Dark Noon
